title: Hymn and Well
premise: Noor Dunmore takes a teaching post in the isolated village of Marrow's End, where enrollment lists include children no one has seen and the old well behind the school refills on its own. When a bell that was melted down in 1911 begins ringing at dusk, Noor learns the village survives by 'counting' one family out of existence each generation to feed the well. Refusing to let her own students be next, she races to smuggle the marked family beyond the parish line before the well refills—ending with Noor taking their place in the count, becoming the new voice of the bell, while the family escapes and the village pretends nothing happened.
about_author: Ada Brightwater is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in villages where records didn't match memories. She writes horror about institutions that keep their own ledgers.

chapters.title: The Enrollment Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor arrives in Marrow's End to teach eleven children, though the village has visibly fewer. The headmaster, Mr. Quill, insists she never amend the ledger, only add names. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: uneasy belonging—she wants this fresh start too badly to question it yet.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Twice
chapters.summary: Noor develops rituals: counting doors, keeping lights burning, noting which children answer roll call. A girl named Sable Ashwin never appears but is always marked present. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: creeping dread as routine becomes evidence that something is being hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor finds the school well bricked over but damp, warm, and humming. Old Sable's grandmother, Widow Ashwin, warns her: 'The well drinks by count.' POV: Noor, with an interlude from Widow Ashwin's 1911 diary. Emotional beat: the first hard truth—the village pays for its survival.

chapters.title: A Bell That Was Never Cast
chapters.summary: At dusk a bell tolls; the church has no bell—it was melted in 1911. Villagers freeze mid-step, then resume as if nothing happened. Quill tells Noor the bell rings 'when the count is near.' POV: Noor. Emotional beat: isolation deepens; she realizes everyone knows except her.

chapters.title: The Marked Family
chapters.summary: Noor discovers the Ashwins are this generation's chosen payment—Sable is on the ledger twice. She confronts Widow Ashwin, who accepts the sacrifice as tradition. POV: alternating Noor and Sable. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—Sable begs to run; her grandmother refuses to shame the village.

chapters.title: Lessons After Dark
chapters.summary: Noor secretly teaches Sable the roads beyond the parish line, mapping routes by candlelight while the bell tolls closer each night. Other children begin leaving chalk marks on her door—silent offers of help. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: fragile hope; belonging found in conspiracy rather than compliance.

chapters.title: Quill's Confession
chapters.summary: Quill reveals he once tried to save a family decades ago; the well took his daughter instead. The count must be paid or it collects arbitrarily. POV: Quill, then Noor. Emotional beat: grief and complicity—the villain is also a father who broke first.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Count
chapters.summary: The village gathers for the Rite of Tally. Noor forges ledger entries to make it appear the Ashwins already left, buying hours. The bell rings without stopping. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve; there is no turning back now.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Water
chapters.summary: Noor drives the Ashwins through fog toward the parish line as villagers and something wearing villagers' faces pursue. At the boundary stone, Widow Ashwin finally chooses her granddaughter over tradition and crosses. POV: Noor and Sable. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, speed, and the well beginning to refill behind them.

chapters.title: Hymn
chapters.summary: The well refills; someone must be counted. Noor stays so the ledger balances, and at dawn the melted bell rings once—a hymn with her voice in it. Sable, safe beyond the line, keeps her teacher's lessons alive. POV: Sable, closing with Noor's final entry. Emotional beat: sorrowful resolution—survival's price paid willingly, truth carried out of the valley.
